name: Tung Chee Chen
current_role: Former chairman & CEO of Orient Overseas (International) Ltd (OOCL parent); private investor; Monaco's honorary consul in Hong Kong
profile: Second son of shipping magnate C.Y. Tung and younger brother of Hong Kong's first chief executive Tung Chee-hwa. Ran Orient Overseas (OOCL) as chairman/CEO from 1996; in 2018 he and his brother sold the family's 68.7% stake to COSCO for about $4.3bn. Now largely retired from executive roles.
interesting_fact: He trained as an engineer: a bachelor's degree from the University of Liverpool and a master's in mechanical engineering from MIT, before joining the family shipping group.
deep_cut_fact: He has chaired the Institute for Shipboard Education Foundation, which oversees Semester at Sea, the floating-university program his father C.Y. Tung was instrumental in founding.
notes: No personal public channels found. His brother Tung Chee-hwa died in Sept 2026 (per Baird Maritime), so avoid outreach timing insensitivity. Any route would likely be via OOCL/Tung family office; Semester at Sea link is a soft angle.

name: Won-Woo Kim
current_role: President (사장) and head of Digital Strategy, NICE Holdings (largest shareholder of NICE Group), promoted in the 2026 executive reshuffle
profile: Kim Won-woo (김원우, b. ~1993) is the eldest son of NICE Group founder Kim Kwang-soo, who died in 2018 at 55; he inherited control at age 25 and is the largest shareholder of NICE Holdings, parent of Korea's leading credit bureau NICE Information Service. He has worked in the group's digital strategy unit, becoming executive director in Dec 2024 and president for 2026.
interesting_fact: He became controlling owner of one of Korea's biggest credit-information groups at just 25; day-to-day management has been run by professional CEO Choi Young while he built experience in digital strategy.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Korean-language press only. Best route is via NICE Holdings corporate communications.

name: Mark Leonard
current_role: Founder of Constellation Software; former president (stepped down Sept 2025 for health reasons), left the board May 2026, now adviser on its Permanent Engaged Minority Shareholder (PEMS) strategy
profile: After an MBA from Western Ontario and ~11 years in venture capital, Leonard founded Toronto's Constellation Software in 1995; it has bought 850+ vertical-market software businesses and holds them permanently. He and family own ~7%. He resigned as president in Sept 2025 and did not stand for re-election to the board in May 2026, staying on as an adviser.
interesting_fact: Famously elusive: he has almost never spoken to the press, and before CSI he worked as a banker, valuator, mason, gravedigger, dog handler, bouncer, sapper and wind energy researcher (Globe and Mail via Forbes).
deep_cut_fact: Despite building a multibillion-dollar company, his reported compensation as president was a symbolic C$1 base salary with no bonus or stock awards.
notes: Extremely private; famously never gives interviews; stepped back for health reasons in 2025, so an interview request is unlikely to succeed. His annual President's letters (csisoftware.com) are the best way to show familiarity. Route via Constellation corporate.

name: Xue Min
current_role: Founder and chairman of United Imaging Group (联影集团), controlling shareholder of Shanghai United Imaging Healthcare (688271.SS)
profile: Xue Min (薛敏, b. 1957) studied physics at Fudan and earned an MRI-physics master's in Wuhan before PhD studies in biomedical engineering at Case Western Reserve/Cleveland Clinic. He founded Shenzhen Mindit (MRI) in 1998, later sold to Siemens, then in 2011 founded United Imaging to challenge GE, Siemens and Philips; it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2022.
interesting_fact: United Imaging set out from day one to develop every product line and core technology in-house; within about a decade it had launched over 260 products, including China's own 1.5T MRI magnet.
deep_cut_fact: After 100-plus days of intensive work, United Imaging's very first image, produced in 2011-12, was a scan of Xue Min's own right foot.
notes: Chinese-language press mostly. Zhang Qiang is chairman/CEO of the listed United Imaging Healthcare; Xue chairs the parent group. IR email is the listed company's.

name: Mark Davis
current_role: Owner and managing general partner, Las Vegas Raiders (NFL); owner, Las Vegas Aces (WNBA)
profile: Son of Raiders legend Al Davis, Mark Davis spent his whole career inside the team, starting in the equipment room and team retail, and inherited control after his father's death in 2011. He moved the franchise from Oakland to Las Vegas in 2020 and Allegiant Stadium; the team is now valued at over $7bn (vs $761m in 2011). He bought the WNBA's Aces in 2021.
interesting_fact: While working in Raiders team retail he is said to have invented the muff-style hand warmer now used across the NFL.
deep_cut_fact: A Chico State alumnus, he long kept driving from Oakland back to Chico to see his favourite barber for his trademark bowl cut, and famously drove a 1997 Dodge Caravan with a VHS player.
notes: Approachable, unpretentious reputation but gives few long interviews (ESPN's Tim Keown profile is a rare one). Aces dynasty (WNBA titles) and Las Vegas stadium economics are natural podcast angles. Route via Raiders communications department.

name: Adam Kwok
current_role: Executive director, Sun Hung Kai Properties (since 2014); runs SHKP's South China property business
profile: Adam Kwok Kai-fai (郭基煇) is a grandson of SHKP co-founder Kwok Tak-seng and son of former joint chairman Thomas Kwok. After a stint in investment banking he joined Hong Kong's largest developer in 2008, became an executive director in 2014 and has led its South China (mainland) property business since 2013, acting as project director on major residential and commercial schemes.
interesting_fact: He is part of one of Asia's richest property families: four of his cousins, his father, an uncle and his grandmother have all been billionaires.
deep_cut_fact: A keen cyclist, he donated HK$10 million to a Hong Kong Sports Institute / HKUST joint venture to develop more aerodynamic cycling equipment for Hong Kong riders.
notes: Also sits on HK government's Major Sports Events Committee and is a vice president of REDA. Avoid referencing his father's conviction. Route via SHKP corporate communications.

name: Jin Sook Chang
current_role: Co-founder and former chief merchandising officer of Forever 21 (no longer involved since the 2019-20 bankruptcy sale)
profile: Korean-born Jin Sook Chang emigrated to Los Angeles in 1981 with husband Do Won Chang; in 1984 they opened a 900 sq ft store, Fashion 21, in Highland Park and built it into Forever 21, a fast-fashion chain with ~600 stores and 30,000 staff by 2015, where she ran merchandising. The company went bankrupt in 2019 and was sold in 2020; she is no longer listed as a billionaire.
interesting_fact: The couple are devout Christians, which is why 'John 3:16' was printed on the bottom of every Forever 21 shopping bag.
deep_cut_fact: The empire began as a 900-square-foot shop called 'Fashion 21' in LA's Highland Park, opened in 1984 with just $11,000 in savings.
notes: No longer a billionaire (Forbes, July 2019) and no public activity found since 2020; very private. Avoid the bankruptcy as a topic. Profile is shared with husband Do Won Chang. No published contact channels.

name: Nandlal Rungta
current_role: Long-serving director of Rungta Mines Ltd (on the board since January 1985); the group is now chaired by Siddharth Rungta
profile: Nandlal Rungta is the patriarch behind Rungta Mines, a privately held Kolkata/Chaibasa-based iron-ore, manganese and steel group incorporated in 1962 that has expanded into integrated steel plants (five facilities in Odisha, one in Jharkhand), TMT bars under the Rungta Steel brand, construction and power. Day-to-day leadership has passed to the next generation under chairman Siddharth Rungta.
interesting_fact: Rungta Mines is one of India's largest private merchant iron-ore miners yet remains an unlisted company, and has diversified from mining into integrated steelmaking and captive power.
notes: Extremely low public profile; virtually no interviews or press. Wealth lists (360 ONE) now credit 'Siddharth Rungta and family'. Alive status inferred from his still-active directorships (tofler.in), not a dated source. Corporate route only.

name: Wang Jian
current_role: Co-founder and chairman, BGI Group (parent of Shenzhen-listed BGI Genomics, 300676.SZ)
profile: Wang Jian (汪建, b. 1954) trained in medicine in China, did postdoctoral research at the Universities of Texas and Iowa and was a research fellow at the University of Washington (1990-94). He co-founded BGI in 1999 to take on China's share of the Human Genome Project and built it into one of the world's largest genomics groups (sequencing, BGI Genomics, MGI Tech). He also co-founded iCarbonX.
interesting_fact: BGI was founded in 1999 to deliver China's 1% contribution to the international Human Genome Project, and grew into one of the world's largest genome-sequencing organisations.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2024, aged 70, he led a BGI science team to the summit of Everest via the north side, his second ascent 14 years after first summiting with Vanke founder Wang Shi in 2010, setting a record as the oldest Chinese person to summit; the team collected ultrasound and EEG data at the top.
notes: Outspoken, media-friendly in Chinese press; known for extreme-sport stunts (Everest, etc.) used to promote health data science. ir@bgi.com is BGI Genomics' listed IR address, not personal.

name: Kalanithi Maran
current_role: Founder, executive chairman and managing director, Sun TV Network / Sun Group
profile: Son of former Union minister Murasoli Maran, he launched Sun TV in 1993 and built Sun Group into a south-Indian media giant: 37 channels reaching 140m+ households, newspapers, FM radio, DTH, Sun Pictures and a Hindi channel (Sun Neo, 2024). Sun also owns cricket franchises Sunrisers Hyderabad (IPL), Sunrisers Eastern Cape (SA20) and Sunrisers Leeds (The Hundred). He owned SpiceJet 2010-15.
interesting_fact: Sun Group's cricket empire spans three countries: Sunrisers Hyderabad in the IPL, Sunrisers Eastern Cape (SA20 champions) in South Africa and, since 2025, Sunrisers Leeds in England's The Hundred.
deep_cut_fact: After Don Bosco and Loyola College in Chennai, he went to the US for an MBA at the University of Scranton in Pennsylvania, where the abundance of TV channels (vs India's single state broadcaster) is said to have inspired Sun TV.
notes: Rarely gives interviews. tvinfo@sunnetwork.in is Sun TV's general company email from exchange filings (not a dedicated press address). Avoid the family share dispute and old telecom case.
